page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m1.xlarge is a burstable instance type built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.t5-c1m1.xlarge delivers entry-level performance. In CPU-bound workloads, the instance scored 1018.78 in stress-ng single-core tests and 4021.29 in multi-core tests. Memory performance is constrained, with a Passmark memory score of 1082.09 and a read-only large block memory bandwidth of 28.46 GB/sec. However, write bandwidth for large blocks reached 26.9 GB/sec, placing it in the average tier. Cryptographic and compression tasks show lower efficiency, with single-threaded gzip compression at 19.01 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 5.22 GB/sec.

Due to its burstable CPU allocation model, this instance is designed for workloads with low baseline CPU utilization that experience occasional spikes. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio and lack of local storage represent significant tradeoffs, making it unsuitable for memory-intensive databases or high-throughput storage applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile is positioned as a budget-friendly option for lightweight utility tasks. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, development and testing environments, lightweight microservices, and low-traffic applications.

It is configured with 4 vCPUs, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1018.78 and a multi-core score of 4021.29. Large-block memory write bandwidth is average at 26.9 GB/sec, but read bandwidth and database operations remain weak. Given its burstable CPU allocation and low memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is qualitatively cost-effective for low-intensity workloads. It is best suited for lightweight applications, code repositories, development environments, and low-traffic web serving where sustained maximum CPU performance is not required.
